title: search_logged_models ordering: always end with a stable model_id tie-breaker unless the caller sorts by model_id
answers: Why does the order of logged models change between identical searches when several models have the same metric or creation time?
How do I make search_logged_models results stable across pages when user sort keys tie?
Why does sorting logged models by model_id produce a duplicated ORDER BY clause?
body:
Path: mlflow/store/tracking/sqlalchemy_store.py:_apply_order_by_search_logged_models builds the ORDER BY for search_logged_models from the user's order_by list (field_name plus ascending) and then appends default keys. Any change to sort order or paging for logged models goes through this function.
Rule: After the user's keys, append creation_timestamp_ms desc only if the caller did not sort by creation_timestamp_ms, and append SqlLoggedModel.model_id asc only if the caller did not sort by model_id (tracked with has_model_id, mirroring has_creation_timestamp). model_id is the final key, so ties in user sort keys resolve the same way on every page.
Symptom: When user-provided sort keys tied (for example several models with the same metric value), page boundaries were not deterministic, so paginated results could repeat or drop models.
Constraints: Only affects logged-model search ordering. When the caller already sorts by model_id, no extra model_id key is added, so the ORDER BY does not repeat the same column. Verify ORDER BY shape by compiling the query from _apply_order_by_search_logged_models in a test, as the test test_search_logged_models_order_by_model_id_does_not_duplicate_tiebreaker does.
applies: Logged model search ORDER BY construction in the SQLAlchemy tracking store; applies when adding or changing default sort keys for logged models.
says: Model search results shift unpredictably between pages when models share identical sort values.
Identical searches on the model page return items in different orders when scores tie.
Make model list pagination consistent and stable when sorting by creation time or metrics.
Models drop or reappear across pages because secondary sorting is not deterministic.
Prevent model search order from shuffling randomly when several models have identical metrics.
search: In mlflow/store/tracking/sqlalchemy_store.py:_apply_order_by_search_logged_models, logged model searches must append a final SqlLoggedModel.model_id asc tie-breaker unless the caller already sorted by model_id. The builder also appends creation_timestamp_ms desc unless creation timestamp was explicitly specified by the caller. Tracking whether model_id is present prevents duplicated columns in the generated ORDER BY clause while ensuring deterministic page boundaries when user sort keys tie. Applies to ORDER BY construction for search_logged_models queries in the SQLAlchemy tracking store.
